_what: The formats a case-study take may be written in. A take's angle names its format, and the format declares the sections that format requires. scripts/check-take-formats.mjs in ~/Dev/brettmarlin enforces this; skills/ offer this list when prompting for a take.
_why: A take is chosen at authoring time and carries a shape. Before this file the shape was whatever the last take happened to have, which is how convoy's video take was silently skipped by a tool expecting Card/Problem/Role/Outcome. A format that is written down can be asked for, checked, and offered as a menu.
_reader_facing: NEVER. A take is an authoring concept. No reader, recipient, or password-protected bespoke view is ever shown which take they are reading, or that others exist.

decisions-outcomes.label: Decisions and outcomes
decisions-outcomes.purpose: The default framing for public surfaces: what was decided, and what it produced.
decisions-outcomes.audience: hiring managers, prospective clients, anyone arriving cold

public-abstracted.label: The pattern
public-abstracted.purpose: The same work with the client and specifics abstracted to the pattern, so restricted engagements can still be shown.
public-abstracted.audience: public surfaces where the engagement itself is not nameable
sections_optional: A guess that was honest, and still wrong
The same symptom, a different document

recipient-named.label: Named for a recipient
recipient-named.purpose: Written for one named reader, with the detail a cold surface cannot carry.
recipient-named.audience: a single recipient behind a bespoke portfolio

video.label: Video walkthrough script
video.purpose: A spoken walkthrough: a spine, then timed beats with what is on screen and what is said.
video.audience: whoever the recording is sent to
video._note: Not a prose take. It uses `## Beat N — ...` headings rather than `### ` sections, so the prose-shaped checks do not apply to it. Marked here so tools can recognise it deliberately instead of skipping it silently, which is what happened before this file existed.

full-case.label: Full case
full-case.purpose: The whole story told in beats: the narrative walkthrough, one beat at a time, each carrying the image that is evidence for it. What a reader gets when they want the case study rather than the summary of it.
full-case.audience: a fractional client evaluating the work in depth, or any surface where a study has earned the full telling
full-case._note: Beats is what distinguishes this format from decisions-outcomes, where Beats is optional. A full-case take without beats is a decisions-outcomes take that has not admitted it.

short.label: Short
short.purpose: The whole case in six to nine beats. Same framing as decisions-outcomes, edited down to the moments where the work turned, so it is read rather than admired and abandoned.
short.audience: everyone. This is the one that ships once it exists.
short._note: Written by skills/shape-case-study from an existing take, never from scratch. The take it was cut from STAYS in the file: it is the long record and the source for future drafts, and the material dropped on the way here lives there rather than in a graveyard section. Which of the two publishes is published_take, so switching back is one line.
